563: Scope ruling: Commerce properly included green tube for drill pipe within the scope of the antidumping investigation and order, as supported by substantial evidence on the three physical criteria.
Accordingly, Commerce's inclusion of green tube in the scope of the investigation and in the calculation of industry support was supported by substantial evidence and was not contrary to law.
1124: Scope ruling: whether exhibition booth kits of aluminum extrusions and fasteners fall within the AD/CVD orders on aluminum extrusions from China, or within the finished goods kit exclusion
Thus, under Meridian, they do not qualify for the "finished goods kit" exclusion.
1587: Scope ruling: whether curtain wall units and parts of curtain walls fall within the scope of the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on aluminum extrusions from China, including the finished-merchandise exclusion.
This court discerns no flaw in Commerce's determination that Yuanda's curtain wall parts are within the plain language of the Orders.
1934: Whether aluminum trim kits fall within the scope of the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on aluminum extrusions from China, including whether they meet the finished goods kit exclusion's fastener exception.
Substantial evidence supports Commerce's finding that the trim kits meet the exception to the finished goods kit exclusion.
3085: Whether 4.75 mm steel wire rod falls within the scope of the antidumping duty order on steel wire rod through a minor alteration anti-circumvention determination, despite lying outside the order's literal 5.00 mm to 19.00 mm range.
We hold that Commerce's initial minor alteration anti-circumvention determination was in accordance with law and supported by substantial evidence.
4058: Scope ruling: whether imported OCTG that was made from Chinese green tubes but finished in Indonesia falls within the unfinished-OCTG language of the China AD/CVD orders. Court held the merchandise is finished OCTG and cannot be unfinished OCTG under the orders' language.
The imported merchandise is indisputably finished OCTG, and cannot be categorized as unfinished OCTG.
4059: Scope ruling: whether OCTG finished in a non-subject third country (Indonesia) can be treated as from China via Commerce's substantial transformation analysis before any circumvention inquiry under 19 U.S.C. § 1677j. Court held Commerce may use substantial transformation to determine country of origin and vacated and remanded for the Trade Court to review whether Commerce applied it properly.
We conclude that Commerce is entitled to use the substantial transformation analysis to determine country of origin before resorting to the circumvention inquiry.
4875: Whether non-individually investigated separate-rate firms with a zero rate must be excluded from the antidumping duty order (kept inside the order via continuing obligations); court held Commerce reasonably kept them subject to the order.
it is on its face reasonable for Commerce to decide to keep the uninvestigated firms subject to the obligations that accompany inclusion in an order
4876: Whether the voluntary-review firms (which requested individual review and were denied) should be excluded from the antidumping duty order; court held Commerce did not adequately justify including them, so they are outside the order.
We see no reversible error in the Trade Court's conclusion that Commerce did not provide an adequate justification for including the voluntary-review firms in the antidumping duty order in this case.
4908: Scope ruling: whether US&F's AREMA helical spring lock washers fall within the scope of the antidumping duty order on helical spring lock washers from China.
We also find that substantial evidence supports Commerce's final scope ruling that US&F's washers are within the scope of the ADD Order.
4985: Scope ruling: whether STR components in Star Pipe's Joint Restraint Kits (mixed media sets) fall within the antidumping order on steel threaded rod from China
we agree with the Trade Court that substantial evidence supports Commerce's finding that the STR components of Star Pipe's Joint Restraint Kits are within the scope of the STR Order.
5256: Whether Quiedan's rebar agricultural stakes fall within the scope of the antidumping duty order on rebar from China (straight lengths, merchant bar, and intended-use arguments).
The stakes thus clearly have a "straight length."
5356: AD/CVD scope ruling: whether curtain wall units shipped under a full-wall contract fall within the scope of the aluminum extrusions orders or within the finished goods kit exclusion; held inside the orders.
We see neither legal error nor insufficient evidentiary support for the ultimate Commerce determination, and we therefore affirm the Court of International Trade's decision.
5392: Whether imported zinc and nylon masonry anchors fall within the scope of the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on certain steel nails from Vietnam; Commerce's remand determination that they are outside the scope was affirmed.

The Government appeals a decision of the United States Court of International Trade affirming a remand determination of the United States Department of Commerce concluding that certain zinc masonry anchors and certain nylon masonry anchors imported by Midwest Fastener Corp. are outside the scope of certain antidumping and countervailing duty orders
5750: Scope of AD/CVD orders: whether Whirlpool's assembled door handles with end caps fall within the general scope language of the aluminum extrusion orders. Court held the general scope language includes the assembled handles and reversed the CIT on this point.
The general scope language unambiguously includes aluminum extrusions that are part of an assembly.
5751: Scope of AD/CVD orders: whether the handles fall within the finished goods kit exclusion. Court held the exclusion inapplicable because the handles enter assembled, not as a packaged kit.
Because Whirlpool's assembled door handles are not imported in disassembled form, the finished goods kit exclusion is inapplicable.
5752: Scope of AD/CVD orders: whether the fasteners exception in the finished goods kit language extends to the finished merchandise exclusion. Court held Commerce's contrary interpretation was incorrect and the fasteners exception applies only to the kit exclusion.
the fasteners exception only applies to the finished goods kit exclusion and it does not apply to the finished merchandise exclusion.
5785: Scope of AD/CVD orders: Series 6xxx aluminum pallets held within the general scope language of the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on aluminum extrusions from China.
We find no error with that reasonable conclusion, and Perfectus does not dispute it.
5786: Finished merchandise exclusion: pallets made entirely of aluminum extrusions do not qualify for the finished merchandise exclusion and therefore remain within the scope of the orders.
Because the Series 6xxx Pallets are made entirely from aluminum extrusion parts, they do not qualify for the finished merchandise exclusion.
5849: Scope ruling: Commerce's final scope ruling that Sunpreme's solar modules fall within the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on Chinese crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells (substantial evidence review).
we affirm the CIT's conclusion that Commerce's final scope ruling placing Sunpreme's solar products within the ambit of the Orders is supported by substantial evidence.
5858: Scope of the AD/CVD orders on Chinese-cell-free panels assembled in China: Commerce's country-of-assembly test defined the class or kind of merchandise to include solar panels assembled in China with non-Chinese cells, so those panels fall inside the orders.
Commerce's authority to define the class or kind of merchandise within the scope of an order encompasses the authority to determine the country of origin.
6100: AD order scope: whether imported zinc and nylon masonry anchors fall within the scope of the antidumping order on certain steel nails from China; Commerce found them outside the order, affirmed by CIT.
we affirm the decision of the Court of International Trade.
6570: Scope ruling: whether OMG's zinc masonry anchors fall within the scope of the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on certain steel nails. Court held the anchors are unambiguously outside the scope of the orders.
Accordingly, we affirm the decision of the CIT.
6753: Scope ruling: whether Sunpreme's hybrid thin-film solar modules fall within the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on Chinese crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells (CSPV cells, p/n junction, 20-micrometer thickness, thin film exclusion); court held Commerce's scope ruling supported by substantial evidence.
We therefore agree with the CIT that substantial evidence supports Commerce's conclusion that Sunpreme's solar modules contain a p/n junction.
7460: Scope ruling: whether Type B kitchen appliance door handles (aluminum extrusions packaged with plastic end caps and screws) fall within the general scope of the AD/CVD orders on aluminum extrusions from China.

we hold that Commerce's original scope ruling determination that the Type B handles are included within the general scope of the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on aluminum extrusions from China is reasonable and supported by substantial evidence.
7461: Scope exclusion: whether Type B handles are excluded from the orders as finished goods kits, given that the plastic end caps are fasteners.

We also conclude that Commerce's original scope ruling that the Type B handles are not excluded from the scope of the order under the "finished goods kit" exclusion provision is reasonable and supported by substantial evidence.
9064: Circumvention determination under 19 U.S.C. §1677j: Commerce found UAE CORE made from Chinese hot-rolled or cold-rolled steel circumvented the China CORE AD/CVD orders, so the merchandise is subject to the orders; court held substantial evidence supported the pattern-of-trade, level-of-investment, production-process and facilities findings.
We conclude that substantial evidence supports Commerce's determinations as to "pattern of trade," "level of investment," "nature of the production process," and "extent of production facilities."
9152: Scope ruling: Commerce's modification of the quartz surface product scope to exclude only crushed glass products meeting specified criteria was lawful, and the evidence supported that glass products are within the scope of the orders.
Because Commerce has discretion to set the scope of its investigations, Bruskin's hearing request was untimely, and substantial evidence supports Commerce's factual findings, we affirm
9286: Anti-circumvention inquiry: whether Shelter Forest's radiata pine, CARB-certified plywood sold before December 8, 2016 was later-developed merchandise circumventing the AD/CVD orders (negative remand determination affirmed, so merchandise outside the orders).
Commerce's determination that Shelter Forest sold inquiry merchandise prior to December 8, 2016 is both reasonable and supported by substantial evidence.
9761: Whether heat-treated 5050-grade extruded aluminum products of Tai-Ao and Regal fell within the AD/CVD orders' scope (anti-circumvention) for entries made March 21 to November 13, 2016; court held no adequate notice, so suspension of liquidation from March 21, 2016 was not in accordance with law.
Because Commerce did not provide adequate notice to Tai-Ao and Regal until November 14, 2016, Commerce's instructions to suspend liquidation effective March 21, 2016, were not in accordance with law.
10747: Scope ruling: whether CCM's solar panel mounts are within the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on aluminum extrusions from China, including whether they qualify for the finished merchandise or finished goods kit exclusions.
CCM's solar panel mounts are parts or subassemblies and thus cannot be a finished product and cannot qualify for the finished merchandise exclusion.
11813: AD/CVD scope ruling: whether Siffron's plastic shelf dividers containing flexible magnets fall within the Duty Orders on raw flexible magnets from China. Court held Commerce may consult (k)(1) interpretive sources regardless of ambiguity, that InterDesign's reading of flexible magnets was reasonable, and that functional inflexibility was supported by substantial evidence, so the products are outside the order.
we affirm the Trade Court's judgment sustaining Commerce's scope ruling that Siffron's shelf dividers are not covered by the Duty Orders.
12458: Scope ruling: whether Valeo's T-series aluminum sheet falls within the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on common alloy aluminum sheet from China, including whether the 'as designated by the Aluminum Association' language is ambiguous and whether heat-treatment removes the product from the 3XXX-series core.
we affirm the Trade Court's decision sustaining Commerce's remand determination that Valeo's T-series sheets are within the scope of the Orders.
12612: Whether dual-stenciled standard/line pipes fall within the scope of the 1986 Thailand antidumping duty order on standard circular welded carbon steel pipes; Federal Circuit held Commerce's scope ruling that they are inside the order was reasonable and supported by substantial evidence, reversing the CIT.
For the foregoing reasons, we hold that Commerce's Scope Ruling that imports of dual-stenciled pipes fall within the scope of the Thailand Order is reasonable and supported by substantial evidence.
12904: Scope of the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on magnesia carbon bricks: whether MCBs with less than five percent added alumina (MAC bricks) fall outside the orders. Court held Commerce applied the wrong legal standard by imposing a five-percent alumina threshold that expanded the orders contrary to Fedmet I, so the bricks are outside the scope.

Thus, Commerce applied the wrong legal standard by going beyond the meaning given to the term "magnesia carbon bricks" and unlawfully expanding the scope of the orders, as interpreted in Fedmet I, to include Fedmet's MAC bricks with less than five percent alumina.
12933: Scope ruling: whether imported door thresholds fall within the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on aluminum extrusions from China, based on the subassemblies provision of the scope.
The agency's finding that Appellees' door thresholds are subassemblies is an independent basis for sustaining its in-scope determination.
13639: Scope ruling: whether Vandewater's steel branch outlets fall within the antidumping duty order on butt-weld pipe fittings; held within the order.
We affirm the CIT's Final Decision sustaining Commerce's Remand Results that Vandewater's steel branch outlets are within the scope of the ADD Order.
13640: (k)(0) threshold step: whether the scope term butt-weld pipe fittings is unambiguous under industry usage; held ambiguous, so industry usage was properly addressed at (k)(2).
we hold that the term butt-weld pipe fittings in the ADD Order is ambiguous.
13641: (k)(1) analysis: whether the (k)(1) sources dispositively placed the product inside or outside the order; held non-dispositive, so Commerce must consider the (k)(2) criteria.
substantial evidence leads to only one conclusion: the (k)(1) sources are non-dispositive.
13851: Scope ruling: whether Canvas Banner Matisse fabric rolls fall within the antidumping order on artist canvas from China, decided under the 19 C.F.R. 351.225(k)(1) analysis.
As set forth above, Commerce's Final Scope Ruling was supported by substantial evidence, reached upon a proper (k)(1) analysis, did not unlawfully expand the scope of the Order
14417: Whether xanthan gum imported from China via India was covered merchandise within the AD order, given appellants' changed-circumstances argument and Customs' decision not to refer the matter to Commerce; court held no abuse of discretion in declining referral and that the merchandise was covered.

Accordingly, we agree with the trial court and hold it was not an abuse of discretion for Customs to decline to refer Appellants' request for review by Commerce where it reasonably concluded changed circumstances sufficient to warrant a review did not exist.
